synopsis: v0.7.0 1.A.10: ACP server + client surface. `acp serve` binds the HTTP/SSE transport; `acp request` drives a one-shot session/message round-trip

`session/create`. Prints the new session_id
`session/delete :id`

`message/send :id <text>`. Streams events to stdout, one per line, JSON-encoded. Exits when the stream ends
Bind the HTTP/SSE transport to a TCP port and serve sessions

Show the per-adapter health a RUNNING gateway has observed

v0.8.1 U7: manage scheduled cron jobs (add / list / remove / enable / disable). Persists to `$WAYLAND_HOME/cron/jobs.json`; the background runner spawned at session boot picks up changes on its next tick
Add a new job. Exactly one of `--slash`, `--channel`, or `--skill` must be provided (with matching companion flags)
Spawn the cron runner as a detached background daemon
Disable a job by id (kept on disk, skipped by the runner)
Enable a job by id
Print the last N fire records for a job (timestamp, outcome, duration, error message if any). Records come from the JSONL ring-buffer written by the runner alongside jobs.json
List every persisted cron job

Tail recent log lines associated with a job's fires. Currently surfaces fire records from the history file (same data as `cron history`) formatted as structured log lines compatible with the engine's tracing output
Publish an event topic, firing every job with a matching `--trigger event:TOPIC`
Remove a job by id
Print full details for one job: id, expression, target, state, created_at, last_fired, and the outcome of the most recent fire attempt (success + duration, or error message)

Crucible (Mixture-of-Providers): run the cross-provider council over a task. N proposers (each pinned to its own provider from `[providers]`) answer in parallel; a fenced, read-only aggregator fuses them. Requires `[crucible] enabled = true` with a `proposers` roster in your config

FluxRouter web_fetch (`POST /v1/fetch`): fetch a URL and print it as markdown. `--render` selects the JS-rendered premium arm. A free / paid-but-uncleared Flux key returns an `upgrade_required` message — web_fetch is a paid-only capability

Anvil (gated forge) — forge a candidate that passes a REAL executable gate (tests / build / lint), then stamp a verified receipt. Requires ON by default; `[anvil] enabled = false` is the kill-switch. Empty gate config auto-detects the workspace suite
F24-B: the persistent gateway runtime — install / uninstall / start / stop / restart / status / drain, plus the `run` verb every generated launchd, systemd and scheduled-task unit invokes
Close admission, finish in-flight work within a budget, and exit
Register the gateway as a per-user native service for this platform
Stop then start. A stop refusal because nothing was running is not an error here — restarting a stopped gateway is a start
The long-lived runtime itself. This is what every generated service unit invokes; it is not normally typed by an operator
Start the registered gateway through the platform's service manager
Report what the gateway is doing
Stop it through the platform's service manager
Remove the native service registration

F22-04: durable Goals and their Fleet task ledger — open / task / run / status / exec-task. `run` recovers a killed Goal, revokes expired claim leases, drains completions the dead parent never observed, and drives the remaining tasks through the Fleet dispatcher
Count the effects on disk: total, and how many carry distinct labels
The effect boundary: idempotency gate, then the operator's command
Authorize a durable Goal
Recover, reclaim and drive the Goal's tasks through the Fleet dispatcher
The canonical JSON projection of a Goal and its task ledger
Declare a task in the Goal's durable ledger

FluxRouter image generation (`POST /v1/images/generations`). Writes the decoded image to `--out` (or stdout when piped). A free / paid-but-uncleared Flux key returns a `premium_locked` message — image generation is a paid-only capability

F23-06 (Phase 23B): the persistent repository index — `build`, `status`, `search` and `verify`. Every verb prints greppable `F23_INDEX=` lines to STDOUT; `verify` exits 6 when the store disagrees with the working tree
Build or incrementally refresh the index
Bounded hybrid retrieval: BM25 plus symbol lookup, reciprocal-rank fused, with an exact-search fallback
Report record count, on-disk size, scope identity and staleness
Compare the store against the working tree without modifying it
